headline: Kohat Police Lines Attack Kills at Least 22; Higher Toll of 31 Reported
seoTitle: Kohat Police Lines Attack: At Least 22 Dead, Higher Toll Reported | FMB News
seoDescription: Pakistani authorities said the Kohat Police Lines clearance operation ended with eight attackers killed. Reported death tolls ranged from 22 to at least 31.
deck: Police said the overnight clearance operation ended after eight attackers were killed. Pakistani hospital and police-linked reporting places the death toll at 22, while AFP separately cited a senior police official reporting 31; the discrepancy remains unresolved.
author: FMB News World Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Pakistani police and security forces said they completed a roughly 21-hour clearance operation at the Old Police Lines complex in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque during Friday prayers and gunmen entered the compound.
The Central Police Office said eight attackers were killed during the response, according to Dawn and Geo News.

sections.heading: Casualty figures remain inconsistent
paragraphs: Geo News reported, citing hospital officials, that 22 people were killed, including 16 police personnel, and 103 were injured. Dawn earlier reported 21 deaths and more than 100 wounded based on the district health officer and senior police officials.

AFP later cited a senior police official who put the death toll at at least 31, including 16 police personnel, with more than 100 injured. Reuters separately carried AFP’s higher figure. FMB News has not found a published official reconciliation explaining the difference, so the 31 figure is presented as a reported higher toll rather than a settled count.

sections.heading: Responsibility
paragraphs: AFP and Dawn reported that a local militant faction linked to the Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility. FMB News has not independently authenticated the claim and does not present attribution as established beyond those reports.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The compound houses police and counterterrorism offices and residences in a province that has faced repeated militant violence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The attack directly targeted security institutions and the families living within the Police Lines complex, while casualty reporting remained unsettled across authoritative and independent sources.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a final casualty reconciliation from Pakistani authorities, identification of victims and attackers, forensic findings, and any formal government attribution backed by evidence.

verificationNotes: Geo News and Dawn report that police and security forces completed the clearance operation and killed eight attackers.

Hospital and police-linked reporting in Pakistan places the toll at 22 dead and 103 injured, while AFP cited a senior police official reporting at least 31 dead. The discrepancy is explicitly preserved rather than silently choosing one figure.
Reuters independently carried AFP’s higher toll, and AP independently reported the attack and completed standoff with a lower casualty figure.
Claims of responsibility are attributed to reporting and are not independently authenticated by FMB News.
The image is Theshayanahmad’s own 2016 photograph of Kohat on Wikimedia Commons, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0, and is clearly captioned as contextual rather than depicting the attack.
